title: The 80/20 Rule
hook: Most of your money probably comes from a handful of customers. Your calendar doesn't reflect that.
statement: Roughly 80 percent of your results come from about 20 percent of your efforts, customers, or products.
explainer: Everyone knows this rule. Almost nobody acts on it. They still spread time evenly, like every customer and task matters the same. Find your top 20 percent and protect it.
sop: Sort customers, products, or tasks by what they bring in.
Check whether it's 80/20, 90/10, or even more lopsided.
Put more time and money behind the top tier.
Trim or simplify the long tail.
equation_example: 20 customers, $100,000 in revenue. The top 4, that's 20%, bring in $80,000, so 80% of output. More lopsided, like 90/10, means more leverage but more risk if one leaves. Closer to 50/50 is steadier, but there's no obvious lever.
question: Write down your top 20% of customers or tasks, then block time for them this week.
closing_statement: Not all effort earns the same return.
caption:
Principle Nº 286: The 80/20 Rule

Most of your money probably comes from a handful of customers. Your calendar doesn't reflect that.

Roughly 80 percent of your results come from about 20 percent of your efforts, customers, or products.

Your turn: Write down your top 20% of customers or tasks, then block time for them this week.
